Set.14.feature.TFT14_CHANGE_DESC_1: Hacking can happen anytime and in any round!\nIf the Encounter is hacked, you will get a hacked champion card, and if the Common Pick round is hacked, your champion may turn into anvils. Also, if the Creep round is hacked, you will get a <tagArea>unstable item</tagArea> or a dragon egg that turns into a new crafted item every Champion round.
Set.14.feature.TFT14_CHANGE_DESC_2: When an augmentation round is hacked, the augments on the left will change to match the theme.\nSome augments that disappeared in previous seasons will appear, giving a refresh and additional gold.
Set.14.feature.TFT14_CHANGE_DESC_3: Another round of augmentation hacks will have you choose between one augmentation of a higher level and two augmentations of a lower level. If you choose the two lower augmentations, you will have up to four augmentations.

Set.15.feature.TFT15_CHANGE_DESC_3: With the change in mana regen, items have also been reworked. Starting mana is no longer present, and mana regen is now per second.

Set.18.feature.TFT18_CHANGE_DESC_1: TFT is moving to Unreal Engine as a long-term project. Cosmetics such as tacticians, arenas, and booms will move over gradually, and a dedicated PC client is planned for October.
Set.18.feature.TFT18_CHANGE_DESC_2: Wisps appear in the rightmost shop slot every other round during the planning phase. Buy up to one per round for combat, shop, gold/XP, item, and other effects.
Set.18.feature.TFT18_CHANGE_DESC_3: Blossom, Riftbeast, Elderwood, Sprykin, Coven, and other new traits create more flexible pivots and high-roll moments.

Set.18.preview.traitHighlightBlossomDesc: A Wisp-focused vertical that upgrades Wisps, adds them to more shops, grants gold on purchase, and can raise the round limit.
Set.18.preview.traitHighlightCovenDescri: Collect essence from takedowns or losses, then decide whether to cash out or push for a larger reward.
Set.18.preview.traitHighlightDescription: Start with eight signature mechanics, then browse all 36 origins and classes with their champions and breakpoint effects.
Set.18.preview.traitHighlightElderwoodDe: Earn placeable plants such as Stonebark Tree and Lifeblossom. Positioning determines your frontline and support pattern.
Set.18.preview.traitHighlightEldritchDes: Sacrifice a unit on an Eldritch hex at combat start to empower the team; higher breakpoints can keep the sacrifice alive.
Set.18.preview.traitHighlightInfernoDesc: Inferno applies burn and wound effects, and later breakpoints can ignite shop slots to show units one tier higher.
Set.18.preview.traitHighlightRiftbeastDe: Choose an Alpha Mark holder to grant a unique empower effect. Elder Dragon takes two unit slots and counts as two Riftbeasts.
Set.18.preview.traitHighlightRivalDescri: Rengar and Kha'Zix reward solo deployment with takedown stacks, then convert those stacks into gold, team power, or evolutions.
Set.18.preview.traitHighlightSprykinDesc: BFF Willump returns as a mount for Sprykin riders, granting health and attack speed with teamwide bonuses at higher breakpoints.
Set.18.preview.wispCatalogDescription: Explore all {count} Wisps coming in Set 18 by category.
Set.18.preview.wispCategoryDescription: Wisps are grouped into Champion, Combat, Misc, Shop, Gold/XP, Risky, and Item categories, with colors that make them easier to scan.
Set.18.preview.wispDescription: Wisps are one-time shop effects inspired by Charms, redesigned for Enchanted Wilds.
Set.18.preview.wispPurchaseDescription: You can buy up to one Wisp each round. If you skip it, the unit hidden behind the Wisp is revealed after planning.
Set.18.preview.wispScalingDescription: As the game progresses, Wisps become stronger and more expensive. After Stage 5, every other Wisp offer is a Combat Wisp.
Set.18.preview.wispTimingDescription: Wisps appear in the rightmost shop slot every other round and can only be purchased during the planning phase.
